newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Man charged over Australian gem shooting.
newsitem.headline: Man charged over Australian gem shooting.

text.p: A man appeared in court on Thursday charged with two counts of murder after a shooting at a gem business that left two members of a Cambodian refugee family dead and a third critically injured.
Manuel Adajian, 41, was charged with the murder of Lean Thoeun Pin, 49, and his 21-year-old son Virayuth at a city-centre office building on Wednesday.
He was also charged with the attempted murder of Pin's wife, Siv Eng, 44, and with stealing jewellery.
Police said it was alleged Adajian, a jeweller in the same building, had entered the Pin family business to make a partial payment on a debt.
An argument developed and Adajian produced a pistol and fired nine shots, shooting all three, police added. He was arrested at the scene.
Adajian was remanded in custody to appear again in April.
The victims were all members of a family of Cambodian refugees who came to Australia in 1983.

Victorian state parliamentarian Hong Lim, a Cambodian community leader, said on radio the Pins had fled the killing fields of Pol Pot into Thailand and waited in a refugee camp before being sponsored by relatives to settle in Australia.
"Like other refugees, Australia is their haven away from all those horrible things that happened," Lim said. "They saw the country here as giving them another opportunity."
Pin had worked as a tram driver and small-scale gem trader, operating out of his home, before achieving his ambition of opening an office in the city, Lim said.
